result:
Round 198 is planned: it fixes C-R196-02, the open Medium where keyboard focus in the Video row is hidden under the sticky timeline strip at 1280×720. The decision in `b-next.json` is **CONTINUE**.

**What round 197 settled (from C's evidence only)**
- C passed round 197 with real browser checks (`browserVerified=true`), and root published it as `2505252`. Round 198 starts from that commit with a clean tree.
- **SABA-B-4 stage 1 (Studio) is done.** C-R196-01 and the five findings set to close on stage 1 are closed, plus the Studio half of GLOBAL-FOCUS-VISIBLE-UNLAYERED.
- **C-R196-02 is still open.** A's round-197 fix (R89) was reverted under its stop rule, and C confirmed the bug is still there.
- New Low C-R197-01 (markers placed very close together) went to `deferred_low_polish`, which now has 272 entries.
- A's two extra classes on the marker flag (`isolate`, `-z-1`) are accepted as part of R88.

**Why C-R196-02 comes before the regression round:** the last regression was 2026-10-24 and this planning ran on 2026-10-26 at 22:34 UTC, so it is not due yet. The bug gate puts Mediums first. This differs from round 197's §7, which assumed planning on the 27th; `b-round-197.md` records the deviation. The order is now 198 C-R196-02, 199 regression, 200 RETRO, 201 SABA-B-4 stage 2 (store pages).

**How I chose the fix.** I ran live browser probes with injected CSS or JS only, no source change; scripts and results are in `b-round-197/`:

| Approach | Hidden stops | Chrome focus or F2 while scrolled |
|---|---|---|
| Current code | 6 | no jump |
| `scroll-margin` | 6 (Chromium 143 ignores it when focus scrolls an element into view) | no jump |
| `scroll-padding` (the reverted R89) | 0 | jumps to the top |
| `scroll-padding` + negative margin on the chrome | 0 | F2 and Tab through the chrome still jump |
| Keyboard-only reveal | 0 | no jump; mouse clicks never scroll |

**Round 198 task (R91):**
- One React `onFocus` handler on the timeline scroller, plus a new pure helper `app/lib/arrangement/focus-reveal.ts`.
- It acts only when focus came from the keyboard and the target is outside the sticky strip. It scrolls up just enough to show the control, vertically only.
- Round 197's ban on a focus handler is lifted explicitly for this one handler. Every other scroll mechanism stays forbidden, and there is a stop rule if hidden stops remain.
- My probe used a plain browser listener. Only A's live proof will confirm the React handler behaves the same.
- A owns 3 existing files and 2 new ones; the other 1027 tracked files are frozen and hash-checked.
- Tests: FRU-1..5 for the helper, FR-a..e replacing the three placeholder tests, and five mutants.
- C checks 11 rows at both viewports, including chrome focus, mouse clicks, follow mode and the marker menu. Ableton parity does not apply (the Live 12 manual says nothing about this).

**Also done:**
- `tasks/round-197.md` is an exact copy of the previous task.
- I updated `backlog.json` and `feature-status.md`, and wrote `b-round-197.md` and `b-next.json`.
- I made no app-source edits; `git status` was empty when I finished.
- I asked root for a bounded, non-blocking frontend-architect checkpoint at this stage boundary. It covers whether the Studio focus code should stay in `StudioWorkspace.tsx`, and whether the focus tests that count exact strings in the source should become behaviour checks.
- The advisor was available and I called it twice, before and after writing. I adopted both rounds of advice.
